nodes.summary: The witness decoder reads a list $w$ of bits as a list of natural numbers. On the empty list it returns the empty list. Otherwise it reads a unary number $v$ from the front of $w$, a run of $v$ copies of true ended by false, and if decoding the remaining bits gives a list $p$, it returns $v$ followed by $p$. It fails if no unary number can be read from a nonempty list, or if decoding the remaining bits fails.
nodes.title: Witness decoder

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula with $m$ clauses and $k$ distinct variables, and write $R(i, l)$ for row vertex $l$ of diamond $i$ in the HAMPATH construction for $\varphi$. A list of vertices $p$ has normal detours when for every clause $j < m$ there is a diamond $i < k$ such that $p$ contains $R(i, 3j + 1), j, R(i, 3j + 2)$ or $R(i, 3j + 2), j, R(i, 3j + 1)$ as consecutive entries.
nodes.title: Normal clause detours

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula with $m$ clauses, and write $T(i)$ for the top of diamond $i$ and $R(i, l)$ for its row vertex $l$. The arcs of diamond $i$ for variable $x$ are $T(i) \to R(i, 0)$, $T(i) \to R(i, 3m)$, $R(i, 0) \to T(i + 1)$ and $R(i, 3m) \to T(i + 1)$; for every $l < 3m$, both $R(i, l) \to R(i, l + 1)$ and $R(i, l + 1) \to R(i, l)$; and for every clause $j < m$, the arcs $R(i, 3j + 1) \to j$ and…
nodes.title: Arcs of a variable diamond

nodes.summary: For all lists $E$ and $E'$ of pairs of natural numbers, the bit encoding of the concatenation of $E$ and $E'$ is the bit encoding of $E$ followed by the bit encoding of $E'$.
nodes.title: Bits of concatenated edge lists

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $u, v$ and a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers, the bit encoding of the edge list whose first edge is $(u, v)$ and whose remaining edges are $E$ is: $u$ copies of true, then false, then $v$ copies of true, then false, then the bit encoding of $E$.
nodes.title: Bits of an edge list, first edge first

nodes.summary: The edge-list bit encoding of the empty list of edges is the empty bit string.
nodes.title: Edge bits of the empty edge list

nodes.summary: For a natural number $v$ and a list $p$ of natural numbers, the witness encoding of the list with first entry $v$ followed by $p$ is the bit string made of $v$ copies of true, then one false, then the witness encoding of $p$.
nodes.title: Witness encoding of a nonempty list

nodes.summary: The witness encoding of the empty list of vertices is the empty bit string.
nodes.title: Witness encoding of the empty list

nodes.summary: The witness encoding of a list $p$ of natural numbers (the vertices of a candidate path) is the bit string obtained by writing each entry $v$ of $p$, in order, as $v$ copies of true followed by one false, and concatenating the results.
nodes.title: Witness encoding

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula and let $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ be its distinct variables, in the order of the distinct-variable list of $\varphi$. The arcs of the construction for $\varphi$ are the arcs of diamond $i$ for variable $x_i$, for $i = 0, \dots, k - 1$, concatenated in this order.
nodes.title: Arcs of the HAMPATH construction

nodes.summary: The decision problem that accepts a bit string $x$ exactly when, for some $s$, $t$, $n$ and list of pairs $E$, $x$ is the PATH encoding of $s$, $t$ and the digraph on $0, \dots, n - 1$ with edge list $E$, and this digraph has a Hamiltonian path from $s$ to $t$.
nodes.title: The HAMPATH problem

nodes.summary: The list of the distinct variables of a CNF formula $\varphi$, in order of occurrence in $\varphi$, with each variable kept at its last occurrence.
nodes.title: Distinct variables of a formula

nodes.summary: In the HAMPATH construction with $m$ clauses, for every diamond $i$ and every $l \le 3m$, row vertex $l$ of diamond $i$ is a smaller number than the top of diamond $i + 1$.
nodes.title: Row vertices lie below the next top

nodes.summary: In the HAMPATH construction with $m$ clauses, write $T(i)$ for the top of diamond $i$. Row vertex $l$ of diamond $i$ is the number $T(i) + 1 + l$; the row of diamond $i$ consists of the vertices with $l \le 3m$.
nodes.title: Row vertices of a diamond

nodes.summary: In the HAMPATH construction with $m$ clauses, if $i \le i'$ then the top of diamond $i$ is at most the top of diamond $i'$.
nodes.title: Tops are monotone in the diamond index

nodes.summary: In the HAMPATH construction with $m$ clauses, the top of diamond $i$ is the vertex $m + i(3m + 2)$; it is also the bottom of diamond $i - 1$.
nodes.title: Tops of the diamonds

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of pairs of natural numbers, viewed as the digraph on $0, \dots, n - 1$ whose arcs are the pairs in $E$ with both ends below $n$. A list $p$ is a Hamiltonian path from $s$ to $t$ when it lists each of the vertices $0, \dots, n - 1$ exactly once, starts at $s$, ends at $t$, and each two consecutive entries of $p$ form an arc.
nodes.title: Hamiltonian paths

nodes.summary: The encoded PATH instance on the two vertices $0$ and $1$, with no arcs, whose source and target are both $0$.
nodes.title: A fixed HAMPATH no-instance

nodes.summary: A bit string $x$ that decodes to a CNF formula $\varphi$ is sent to Sipser's HAMPATH instance of $\varphi$, and a bit string that does not decode to a CNF formula is sent to the fixed HAMPATH no-instance (two vertices, no arcs, source and target $0$).
nodes.title: The SAT-to-HAMPATH reduction map

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula with $m$ clauses, numbered $0, \dots, m - 1$, and let $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ be its distinct variables, in the order of their last occurrences in $\varphi$ (clauses read in order, and the literals of each clause in order). Put $T_i = m + i(3m + 2)$ and $R_{i,l} = T_i + 1 + l$. The result is the encoded PATH instance with vertices $0, \dots, T_k$, source $T_0$, target $T_k$, and, for…
nodes.title: Sipser's HAMPATH instance of a CNF formula

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, every list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers and every list $p$ of natural numbers, the arc check of $p$ against $n$ and $E$ returns true if and only if every two consecutive entries $u, v$ of $p$ form an arc of the digraph on $0, \dots, n - 1$ listed by $E$, that is, $(u, v) \in E$, $u < n$ and $v < n$.
nodes.title: Checking a vertex list against the arcs

nodes.summary: Given $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers, the arc check of a list $p$ of natural numbers returns true when every two consecutive entries $u, v$ of $p$ satisfy $(u, v) \in E$, $u < n$ and $v < n$, and false otherwise; in particular every list with fewer than two entries passes.
nodes.title: Arc check of a vertex list

nodes.summary: For every list $p$ of natural numbers, the witness decoder applied to the witness encoding of $p$ (each entry $v$ written as $v$ copies of true followed by false) succeeds and returns $p$.
nodes.title: Decoding inverts the witness encoding

nodes.summary: For every list $w$ of bits and every list $p$ of natural numbers, the witness decoder returns $p$ on $w$ if and only if $w$ is the witness encoding of $p$, which writes each entry $v$ of $p$ as $v$ copies of true followed by false.
nodes.title: The witness codec

nodes.summary: The witness decoder succeeds on the empty list of bits and returns the empty list of vertices.
nodes.title: Decoding the empty witness

nodes.summary: If a list $w$ of bits is nonempty and reading a unary number (a run of true ended by false) from the front of $w$ fails, that is, every bit of $w$ is true, then the witness decoder fails on $w$.
nodes.title: Witness decoding fails on a cut-off first number

nodes.summary: If reading a unary number from the front of a list $w$ of bits returns $v$ with remaining bits $r$, that is, $w$ is $v$ copies of true, then false, then $r$, then the witness decoder succeeds on $w$ exactly when it succeeds on $r$, and its result on $w$ is $v$ followed by its result on $r$.
nodes.title: Decoding peels off the first number

nodes.summary: For lists $p$ and $p'$ of natural numbers, the witness encoding of the concatenation of $p$ and $p'$ is the witness encoding of $p$ followed by the witness encoding of $p'$.
nodes.title: The witness encoding respects concatenation

nodes.summary: For every bit string $w$ and every list $p$ of natural numbers, if the witness decoder returns $p$ on $w$, then $w$ is the witness encoding of $p$.
nodes.title: The witness decoder succeeds only on encodings

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $s$, $t$, $n$, a list $es$ of pairs of natural numbers and a list $p$ of natural numbers, the HAMPATH verifier applied to the PATH encoding of $(s, t, n, es)$ and the witness encoding of $p$ returns the same boolean as the Hamiltonian path check on $n$, $es$, $s$, $t$ and $p$.
nodes.title: The verifier on an encoded instance and witness

nodes.summary: For bit strings $x$ and $w$, the HAMPATH verifier accepts $(x, w)$ if and only if there are natural numbers $s$, $t$, $n$, a list $es$ of pairs of natural numbers and a list $p$ of natural numbers such that $x$ is the PATH encoding of $(s, t, n, es)$, $w$ is the witness encoding of $p$, and $p$ is a Hamiltonian path from $s$ to $t$ in the digraph on $0, \dots, n - 1$ with edge list $es$.
nodes.title: What the HAMPATH verifier accepts

nodes.summary: If the PATH instance decoder fails on a bit string $x$, then for every bit string $w$ the HAMPATH verifier rejects $(x, w)$, that is, returns false.
nodes.title: Instances that do not decode are rejected

nodes.summary: If the witness decoder fails on a bit string $w$, then for every bit string $x$ the HAMPATH verifier rejects $(x, w)$, that is, returns false.
nodes.title: Witnesses that do not decode are rejected

nodes.summary: Given bit strings $x$ and $w$, the verifier decodes $x$ as a PATH instance, consisting of a start vertex $s$, a target vertex $t$, a vertex count $n$ and an edge list $E$, and decodes $w$ as a witness, a list $p$ of natural numbers each written in unary. If both decodings succeed, it accepts exactly when the Hamiltonian path check passes, that is, when $p$ is a Hamiltonian path from $s$ to $t$ in the digraph on…
nodes.title: The HAMPATH verifier

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$, $s$, $t$, every edge list $E$ and every list $p$ of natural numbers, the Hamiltonian path check on $(n, E, s, t, p)$ returns true if and only if $p$ is a Hamiltonian path from $s$ to $t$ in the digraph on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with edge list $E$.
nodes.title: The Hamiltonian path check is correct

nodes.summary: Given a natural number $n$, an edge list $E$, vertices $s$ and $t$ and a list $p$ of natural numbers, the Boolean test that $p$ has no repeated entries, has length $n$, has all entries below $n$, has first entry $s$ and last entry $t$, and that every two consecutive entries $u, v$ of $p$ satisfy $(u, v) \in E$, $u < n$ and $v < n$.
nodes.title: The Hamiltonian path check

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every list $p$ of natural numbers all below $n$, the witness encoding of $p$ has length at most $|p| \cdot n$.
nodes.title: Witness length bound

nodes.summary: For every list $p = (v_1, \dots, v_k)$ of natural numbers, the witness encoding of $p$ has length $\sum_{i=1}^{k} (v_i + 1)$.
nodes.title: Witness length

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $s$, $t$, $n$ and every edge list $E$, the encoding of the PATH instance $(s, t, n, E)$ has length $s + t + n + 3 + \ell$, where $\ell$ is the length of the bit encoding of the edge list $E$.
nodes.title: Length of an encoded PATH instance

nodes.summary: For every list $p$ of natural numbers, the witness encoding of $p$ has length at least $|p|$.
nodes.title: A witness is at least as long as its vertex list

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula with $m$ clauses and $k$ distinct variables, and write $T_i = m + i(3m + 2)$ and $R_{i,l} = T_i + 1 + l$ for the top and the row vertices of diamond $i$. Every Hamiltonian path from $T_0$ to $T_k$ in the digraph on the vertices $0, \dots, T_k$ whose arcs are those of Sipser's construction for $\varphi$ has normal detours: for every clause $j < m$ there is $i < k$ such that…

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$ (the number of clauses) and $i$, write $t_i = m + i(3m + 2)$ for the top of diamond $i$ and $r_{i,l} = t_i + 1 + l$ for its row vertex $l$. If $j < m$ and $(j, v)$ is an arc of Sipser's construction for $\varphi$, then there is $i < k$ with $v = R_{i,3j+1}$ or $v = R_{i,3j+2}$.
nodes.title: Out-neighbours of a clause vertex in Sipser's graph

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula with $m$ clauses, and write $T_i = m + i(3m + 2)$ and $R_{i,l} = T_i + 1 + l$. Let $i$ and $l \le 3m$ be natural numbers, and let $(R_{i,l}, v)$ be an arc of Sipser's construction for $\varphi$. nodes.title: Out-neighbours of a row vertex in Sipser's graph

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula with $m$ clauses and $k$ distinct variables, let $T_i = m + i(3m + 2)$, and let $p$ be a Hamiltonian path from $T_0$ to $T_k$ in the digraph on the vertices $0, \dots, T_k$ whose arcs are those of Sipser's construction for $\varphi$. nodes.title: Consecutive vertices of a Hamiltonian path of Sipser's graph form arcs

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula with $m$ clauses and $k$ distinct variables, and write $R_{i,l} = m + i(3m + 2) + 1 + l$ for row vertex $l$ of diamond $i$. If $j < m$ and $(v, j)$ is an arc of Sipser's construction for $\varphi$, then there is $i < k$ with $v = R_{i,3j+1}$ or $v = R_{i,3j+2}$.
nodes.title: In-neighbours of a clause vertex in Sipser's graph

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula with $m$ clauses, and write $T_i = m + i(3m + 2)$ and $R_{i,l} = T_i + 1 + l$. nodes.summary: Let $x$ and $w$ be bit lists. Start the verifier at its start label, with either value of its Boolean variable, with $x$ on stack $\mathsf{X}$ and $w$ on stack $\mathsf{W}$ (as bit symbols, first bit on top) and all other stacks empty. Then within $100(|x| + |w| + 1)^4$ steps it reaches the label $\mathrm{yes}$ if the Hamiltonian path check accepts $x$ and $w$, and the label $\mathrm{no}$ otherwise.
